topic: MBA Reports: Porter's, SWOT & Financial Ratios

copy.instagram:
Staring at a blank MBA report screen while your coffee goes cold? We’ve all been there. The biggest mistake most students make is treating Porter’s and SWOT like a shopping list. You aren't just listing facts; you're building a business case for a CEO.

Slide 1: The 2:2 Trap. Stop dumping basic SWOT bullet points. If you aren't cross-analyzing internal capabilities against market threats, you’re losing marks.

Slide 2: The First Class Blueprint. Start integrating VRIO core competencies with PESTLE macro-risks. Back it up with hard numbers—think ROIC and EBITDA. If your advice isn't budgeted, it’s just a suggestion, not a strategy.

Slide 3: Need a sanity check? We’ve helped hundreds of MBA students turn 'passable' reports into distinction-level analysis. 

Save this for your next drafting session. Link in bio to get our eyes on your draft today.

copy.facebook:
Late night MBA report stress is real, but let’s be honest: the difference between a mid-range grade and a Distinction usually comes down to how you link your frameworks.

Most students fall into the '2:2 Trap'—listing bullet points in a SWOT table without actually showing how internal strengths combat external threats. It feels like busywork, and markers can tell.

To hit that First Class standard, try this instead:
• Integrate VRIO competencies with PESTLE macro-risks.
• Anchor every strategic recommendation in financial reality (ROIC, EBITDA, and liquidity ratios).
• Include a budgeted implementation roadmap. A strategy without a budget is just a wish list.
